title: The mercy that stays, and walks you all the way home
subtitle: His constant, personal mercy for those who turn to Him
intro: Ar-Raheem (الرَّحِيمُ) means the Especially Merciful, the One whose mercy is constant and reaches His believing servants personally: guiding them in this life and bringing them into Paradise in the next. It tells you that His mercy is not a passing mood but a permanent way He deals with you.

root.sense: From rahma, the tender care pictured in the womb. The form Raheem describes a quality that is steady and lasting, like a craftsman who is skilled every day, not once. So Ar-Raheem is mercy that does not come and go but keeps arriving.

row.title: Forgiveness and acceptance
sub: He forgives because He is Raheem

row.title: His mercy is for better people
His mercy outruns His anger
sub: It waits for anyone who turns

knowing: Ar-Rahman and Ar-Raheem share one root, but they show two sides of mercy. Ar-Rahman is mercy at its most vast, embracing every creature. Ar-Raheem is mercy as a constant trait, steady and personal. {idea}Many scholars say Ar-Rahman is His mercy for all, and Ar-Raheem His mercy carried especially to the believers.{/idea} The Quran says plainly that He is, to the believers, Raheem (33:43).

Notice how often this name comes last. He is Ghafur and Raheem, Tawwab and Raheem, Ra'uf and Raheem. The order teaches something: His forgiveness, His acceptance of repentance and His gentleness all grow out of His mercy. He forgives because He is Raheem, the way a strong person can lift and run because he is strong. The Prophet ﷺ conveyed that Allah said, My mercy prevails over My anger (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

His mercy is unlike ours. Human mercy tires, runs out, or turns into resentment when it is not repaid. {idea}His mercy is not a reaction to anything in us; it is who He is.{/idea} When the Prophet ﷺ saw a mother among the captives clutch her baby to her chest, he asked whether she would ever throw her child into a fire, and said that Allah is more merciful to His servants than she is to her child (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).
seeing: The greatest mercy Ar-Raheem gives in this world is guidance. The Quran calls itself a healing and a mercy for the believers (17:82). Food and shelter reach everyone; but the light that lets you understand your pain, make peace with loss and keep hoping is a special gift. {reward}With it, a believer can be tired, in debt and alone, and still find this life sweet.{/reward}

Ar-Raheem is at work in every story of return. Adam slipped, was taught words of repentance, and was received by the One who is At-Tawwab Ar-Raheem (2:37). Yusuf, standing before the brothers who threw him in a well, told them there was no blame on them that day, and that Allah is the Most Merciful of the merciful (12:92). The Prophet ﷺ said the affair of the believer is amazing: in ease he gives thanks, in hardship he is patient, and both are good for him (Sahih Muslim).
trusting: Because His mercy is constant, you do not have to earn it back from zero every time you fall. {trap}The voice that says you have used up your chances is not describing Allah.{/trap} Ar-Raheem is the name that keeps the door open after the tenth failure, the hundredth relapse, the year you stopped praying.

Trusting Ar-Raheem also means trusting His mercy inside what He decrees for you. The test that slows you down, the plan that falls apart, the delay that frustrates you: for a believer, each of these is handled by a Lord who only deals with His servants through mercy. {reward}You can hand Him the outcome and rest, knowing His choice for you is softer than your own would be.{/reward}
loving: A mother's love is the most tender thing we know, and the Prophet ﷺ used it as the smallest measure of Allah's mercy. {reward}When you realise that the One who made you is gentler with you than the one who carried you, love for Him is no longer a duty; it is a homecoming.{/reward}
now: You are sitting in the car outside your house after a day where you lost your temper, skipped a prayer and said something you regret. You feel too dirty to talk to Him. {idea}Ar-Raheem is exactly the name for this moment{/idea}: His mercy did not leave when you did badly, and it is waiting for you before you even turn off the engine.
old: I feel I have to become a better person before Allah will show me mercy again.
new: Ar-Raheem's mercy is steady and already reaching for me; turning back is how I step into it.
try: Read the opening of Surah Al-Fatiha slowly today and pause at Ar-Rahman Ar-Raheem, letting each name sink in on its own.

dua.text: Ya Raheem, Your mercy has never left me. Keep it with me when I am weak, guide me with it when I am lost, and bring me by it into Your Paradise.
dua.note: Call on Him as Ar-Raheem whenever shame makes you want to hide; it is the name that brings forgiveness and acceptance with it.

pairs.why: Ar-Rahman is mercy vast enough for all creation; Ar-Raheem is that mercy made steady and personal for the believer.
He is Ghafur because He is Raheem: forgiveness is one of the fruits of His constant mercy.
At-Tawwab Ar-Raheem: He turns the servant back to Him and receives him with mercy.

faq.a: Ar-Raheem means the Especially Merciful, the One whose mercy is constant and lasting. Scholars commonly explain it as His mercy that reaches the believers in particular: guidance, the Quran and forgiveness in this life, and Paradise in the next.

faq.q: Can a person be called raheem?
faq.a: Yes. Unlike Ar-Rahman, which is for Allah alone, the word raheem can describe people. The Quran itself describes the Prophet ﷺ as kind and merciful to the believers (9:128). Allah's mercy, however, is perfect and unlike any created mercy.

faq.q: Why does Ar-Raheem so often come after other names in the Quran?
faq.a: Ar-Raheem frequently closes a pair, as in Ghafur Raheem and Tawwab Raheem. Many teachers point out that this shows forgiveness, acceptance of repentance and gentleness all flow from His mercy, which the Prophet ﷺ said prevails over His anger.
